english.title: Master of ship / commander of aircraft unload goods for export within the United Kingdom
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were

(A)_[the master of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..) upon which goods ]_
(B)_[the commander of an aircraft, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AIRCRAFT..) upon which goods]_
(C)_[concerned in the unshipping of goods which]_
(D)_[concerned in the relanding of goods which]_
(E)_[concerned in the landing of goods which]_
(F)_[concerned in the unloading of goods which]_
(G)_[concerned in the carrying of goods which]_

had been

(H)_[loaded]_
(I)_[retained]_

for exportation but unloaded in the United Kingdom instead of being exported to and discharged at a place outside the United Kingdom without

(J)_[the authorisation of the proper officer]_
(K)_[payment of the duty chargeable]_
(L)_[repayment of the drawback or allowance paid]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 67(1) and (5) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
were the master of a ship / commander of an aircraft
upon which goods OR
was a person concerned in the
unshipping relanding / landing / unloading / carrying of goods
which had been loaded / retained on board
for exportation but were unloaded in the United Kingdom
without the authorisation of the proper officer OR
payment of duty chargeable OR
repayment of drawback / allowance paid

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Any goods in respect of which an offence under this section is committed shall be liable to forfeiture.
(ii) This section was amended by Schedule 7 to the Taxation (Cross Border Trade) Act 2020, brought into force on the 31st December 2020 by SI 2020/1642. For any offences committed on or after the 31st December 2020, see offence document H100293 (CJS code CE79381).
